feature: Tiered Alphanumeric Hierarchy and Hard-Wrap Indentation
description: The persistent use of the `\n` character followed by standardized leading spaces to create visual and semantic nesting of legislative sub-clauses.
explanation: Critical for structural fidelity in the `text` field; the data relies on a precise sequence of `\n            (1)` or `\n                    (A)` to denote hierarchy. Without this, synthetic data loses its legal scaffolding. Prevalence is 100% across all sampled bills, distinguishing it from standard prose paragraphing.

description: A semantic pattern where the text describes a transformation of meaning by 'striking' existing text and 'inserting' new phrases.
explanation: This feature defines the 'Conflict' between the status quo and the bill's intent within the `text` field. It is critical for synthesis because it requires a model to track two versions of a sentence simultaneously. Evidence: `by striking ''set aside'' and all that follows and inserting the following: ''set aside...''` in the 'Operation Lifesaver' bill.

description: The use of specific domain terminology like 'qualified recipient', 'notwithstanding any other provision of law', and 'legal entity' within rigid 'The term means' constructs.
explanation: Distinct to the legal domain of this dataset. Synthetic generation must replicate the specific syntax of definitions to pass as ground truth legislation. Cites: `The term ''operator'' means an individual or legal entity...` and `Notwithstanding section 1342 of title 31...` in the 'Motor Donor Act'.

description: Segments of the `text` field that lack verbs or narrative flow, consisting entirely of numeric legal references and administrative instructions.
explanation: This represents a 'Long-Tail' challenge (prevalence ~25%) where textual coherence is replaced by symbolic mapping. Example: `Section 280C(c)(3)(B)(ii)(II) of such Code is amended by striking ''maximum rate of tax under section 11(b)(1)''`. This is a significant challenge for standard Transformers optimized for natural language.

description: An uncompromising declarative voice that utilizes 'shall' to create mandatory duties and 'may not' for prohibitions, devoid of emotional affect.
explanation: This is the institutional 'voice' of the `text` and `title` fields. Synthesis must avoid sentiment entirely. Prevalence is universal. Evidence: `The Secretary shall, physically inspect, on an annual basis...` or `The Secretary may not award a grant to a State...` in the 'Railroad Safety' bill.

description: The chronological progression of the text from a conceptual name to definitions, followed by operative actions, and concluding with a temporal trigger.
explanation: This flow provides internal coherence across the `text` schema. High-fidelity synthesis requires the model to 'close' the document logically. Cites: Starts with `This Act may be cited as...` and concludes with `This Act shall take effect on the date that is 180 days after...` in the 'Child Nicotine' bill.
